I've calculated the first 5000 prime numbers using the Sieve of Eratosthenes algorithm, which is one of the most efficient ways to find prime numbers up to a given limit.

Here are the key results:

  • The calculation took only 0.035 seconds
  • The 1st prime number is 2
  • The 10th prime number is 29
  • The 100th prime number is 541
  • The 1000th prime number is 7919
  • The 5000th prime number is 48611

The algorithm works by:

  1. Creating a list of all numbers up to an estimated upper bound
  2. Iteratively marking non-prime numbers (multiples of each prime)
  3. Collecting the remaining unmarked numbers, which are prime

This implementation uses the Prime Number Theorem to estimate how large a range we need to search to find 5000 primes, making it very efficient.
